paper.title_en: Short-term power load forecasting using convolutional and quantum long short-term memory networks with attention
paper.abstract_en: Accurate short-term load forecasting (STLF) is crucial for the efficient operation of power systems and intelligent smart grid management. In this work, a novel CNN–QLSTM–Attention framework is proposed, which combines convolutional neural networks for feature extraction, quantum-inspired long short-term memory (QLSTM) for temporal sequence modeling, and an attention mechanism for adaptive feature weighting. The proposed model is evaluated using real-world load demand data and compared with several benchmark deep learning models, including LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, RNN, and 1DCNN. Experimental results demonstrate the superior forecasting capability of the proposed framework, achieving an RMSE of 35.327, MAE of 29.708, MAPE of 2.76%, and an R<sup loc="post">2</sup> value of 0.967. Compared with conventional models, the proposed approach significantly reduces prediction errors while maintaining stable and consistent performance under varying load conditions. Furthermore, rolling window cross-validation and statistical analyses validate the robustness and generalization ability of the model. Overall, the results confirm that the proposed CNN–QLSTM–Attention framework provides an accurate, reliable, and effective solution for short-term load forecasting applications in modern smart grids. •A hybrid CNN–QLSTM–Attention model is proposed for accurate multistep electric load forecasting.•Quantum-inspired LSTM integrates variational quantum circuits to enhance temporal dependency learning.•The attention mechanism improves interpretability by dynamically weighting salient time steps.•Sliding-window multistep forecasting effectively captures long-term consumption patterns.•Experimental results demonstrate significant error reduction compared to classical and hybrid deep learning models.
